82.s: What period is a country's Balance of Payments normally recorded for?
82.x: Balance of Payments (BoP) – A systematic and complete record of all economic transactions between the residents of a country and the rest of the world during a period, normally one year

82.s: What is the systematic record of all import and export transactions of a country in a year called?
82.x: Short form – Systematic record of "all import and export transactions of a country during a given period, normally a year" (goods exports, government-to-government deals or capital movements alone are only parts)

82.s: What are the two main accounts of the balance of payments?
82.x: Accounts – Two main accounts – the current account and the capital account

82.s: Which IMF manual divides the BoP into current, capital and financial accounts?
82.x: IMF BPM6 – Three accounts – current, capital and financial; the RBI generally combines capital and financial under "Capital Account"

82.s: To what does the term Balance of Payments mainly relate?
82.x: Coverage – Visible trade, invisible trade and borrowings; the term relates to exports and imports (foreign trade)

82.s: What does the Balance of Trade cover?
82.x: Coverage – Goods only (visible) – All transactions: goods, services, transfers, income, capital

82.s: What does the Balance of Payments cover, unlike the Balance of Trade?
o: All transactions: goods, services, transfers, income, capital
82.x: Coverage – Goods only (visible) – All transactions: goods, services, transfers, income, capital

82.s: How is the Balance of Trade calculated?
82.x: Formula – Goods exports − goods imports – Whole external account, double-entry

82.s: What does the Balance of Payments record, using double entry?
82.x: Formula – Goods exports − goods imports – Whole external account, double-entry

82.s: Where does the Balance of Trade sit within the BoP?
82.x: Place – Part of the current account – Current + capital/financial account

82.s: Which accounts make up the Balance of Payments?
82.x: Place – Part of the current account – Current + capital/financial account

82.s: Why is the Balance of Trade an incomplete record?
82.x: Picture – Incomplete record – Better, complete picture – covers both visible and invisible items

82.s: Which items does the Balance of Payments cover, giving a complete picture?
82.x: Picture – Incomplete record – Better, complete picture – covers both visible and invisible items

82.s: When is there a Balance of Trade surplus?
82.x: BoT surplus / BoT deficit – Goods exports > goods imports / goods imports > goods exports

82.s: How is a favourable BoP achieved?
o: By raising exports and reducing imports
82.x: Favourable BoP – Achieved by stepping up exports and reducing imports (both)

82.s: Which of these relates directly to the balance of payments?
82.x: Link to reserves – Among CRR, SLR, demonetisation and forex reserves, only foreign currency reserves relate to the BoP – its overall balance shows up as a change in reserves

82.s: Which component forms the largest part of India's forex reserves?

82.s: Where does gold rank among the components of India's forex reserves?
82.x: Gold – Second

82.s: Which component of India's forex reserves comes from IMF allocation and ranks third?

82.s: Which is the smallest component of India's forex reserves, an unconditional drawing right?
82.x: Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in the IMF – Smallest; unconditional drawing right

82.s: Which of these is not part of India's forex reserves?
82.x: Order of share (March 2025): FCA > Gold > SDRs > RTP. Loans from foreign countries or the World Bank, NRI deposits and "fiscal deficit deposits" are outside reserves.

82.s: What is the number of months of imports that forex reserves can pay for called?
82.x: Import cover = months of imports the reserves can pay for.

82.x: US$ 412,871 million at end-March 2019 – RBI, 2018-19

82.s: What was India's rank in forex reserves when they reached $608.99 bn in June 2021?
82.x: $608.99 bn on 25 June 2021 – 5th largest – After China, Japan, Switzerland, Russia (Ministry of Finance)

82.x: $701.4 bn (Jan 2026) – ≈ 94% of external debt

82.x: $682.3 bn (29 May 2026) – ≈ 11 months of import cover

82.s: What was India's rank in forex reserves at the all-time high of $785.71 bn in September 2026?
82.x: All-time high $785.71 bn (15 Sep 2026) – India 4th after China, Japan, Switzerland

82.s: Which country holds the largest official gold reserves (about 8,133 tonnes)?
82.x: Largest official gold reserves: USA (~8,133 tonnes, World Gold Council; Nov 2019 and now).

82.s: What is a current account deficit?
o: Payments exceed receipts from goods, services, transfers and income
82.x: CAD – Payments exceed receipts from goods, services, transfers and net income (excess of total imports over total exports); exporting more does not cause it

82.s: What kind of goods trade balance does India run?
82.x: Trade deficit – India runs a persistent trade deficit in goods; services and remittances only partly offset it

82.x: 1990-91 – 3.1-3.2% of GDP (crisis); IMF drawn in 1991

82.s: How many years had passed since India's previous current account surplus when it recorded one in 2001-02?
82.x: 2001-02 to 2003-04 – Surplus three years running (first in 24 years in 2001-02) – the only such run

82.s: What was India's peak current account deficit in FY13 (taper tantrum year)?
82.x: FY13 – Peak 4.8% of GDP (taper tantrum) – higher than 1990-91

82.x: 2013-14 – Trade deficit, net invisibles positive, capital account in surplus (financed the CAD)

82.s: What was India's current account balance in Q4 2023-24?

82.s: What was India's current account deficit in FY 2025-26?

82.s: What was India's current account deficit in Q1 2026-27?
To what did India's services exports rise in FY24, cushioning the trade deficit?
82.x: FY24 external recovery: moderation in merchandise export growth + sharp decline in import growth; services exports cushioned the trade deficit (up 4.85% to USD 341.06 bn).

82.s: Which of these is a structural cause of India's current account deficit?
82.x: Causes of CAD: structural – oil and gold imports, low export competitiveness, savings-investment gap; cyclical – temporary global slowdown, commodity shocks.

82.s: Which classic item is the largest source of India's net invisibles?
82.x: Largest source of net invisibles (classic items) – Private transfers = foreign remittances

82.s: What share of the merchandise deficit did India's record services surplus of FY25 finance?
82.x: Since the 2010s – Net software services larger still – record services surplus $188.8 bn (FY25), about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit; software = largest part

82.s: How much did India receive in remittances in FY25, as the world's largest recipient?
82.x: World's largest remittance recipient – India (also in 2015): $135.4 bn (3.5% of GDP) in FY25

82.s: Which country was the second-largest remittance recipient in 2024 per the World Bank?
82.x: World Bank 2024 – India $129 bn > Mexico $68 bn > China > Philippines > Pakistan

82.s: Which country was the largest source of India's remittances in the RBI survey 2023-24?
82.x: Sources (RBI survey 2023-24) – USA 27.7% > UAE 19.2% > UK 10.8%

82.s: Who are the largest remitters of money to India?
82.x: Largest remitters – NRIs – ahead of MNCs, foreign banks and tourists

82.s: How do remittances behave over the business cycle?
82.x: Nature – Remittances are counter-cyclical and create no debt; net primary income is an outflow for India

82.s: Which balance is included in the current account?
82.x: Current account – Goods + services + income + transfers; it includes the Balance of Trade; capital receipts and payments lie outside it

82.s: What is an invisible export?
82.x: Invisibles – Services + income + transfers; invisible export = export of services

82.s: Which of these is a non-factor service in the BoP?
82.x: Services – Non-factor (shipping, banking, tourism, software) + factor income

82.s: In which account of the BoP is FDI recorded?
82.x: Capital account – Foreign loans, FDI and portfolio investment; FDI belongs here, while private remittances are current account

82.s: What is exports minus imports of goods and services plus net primary and secondary income called?
82.x: Current-account balance – Exports − imports of goods and services + net primary income + net secondary income

82.s: On which side of the BoP is every inflow of foreign exchange recorded?
82.x: Every inflow / outflow of foreign exchange – Every inflow of foreign exchange = credit side; every outflow = debit (double-entry book-keeping)

82.s: How is a gift received from foreigners recorded in the BoP?
82.x: Gifts (current account) – Gift to foreigners = debit; gift from foreigners = credit

82.s: How are exports of goods and services entered in the BoP?
82.x: Exports of goods/services – Credit

82.s: How is the purchase of foreign assets by residents recorded in the BoP?
82.x: Residents buying foreign assets – Capital-account debit

82.s: How is the sale of Indian assets to foreigners recorded in the BoP?
82.x: Sale of Indian assets to foreigners – Credit

82.s: In which BoP account are software services exports recorded?
82.x: Software services exports – Current account (services)

82.s: In which BoP account are foreign loans, FDI and FPI recorded?
82.x: Foreign loans, FDI, FPI – Capital account

82.s: Where in the BoP are private remittances recorded?
82.x: Private remittances – Current account – secondary income (transfers)

82.s: Under which head of the BoP are crude oil imports recorded?
82.x: Crude oil imports – Merchandise trade

82.s: What is always true of the BoP in accounting terms?
82.x: Current + Capital + Financial account + Net Errors & Omissions = 0 – the BoP always balances in accounting terms; a surplus in one account = deficit in another. The BoT need not balance.

82.s: What are BoP transactions that happen for their own sake ("above the line") called?
82.x: Autonomous transactions ("above the line") happen for their own sake; accommodating ones ("below the line") fill the gap – official reserve changes, official borrowing.

82.s: What does a positive overall BoP do to forex reserves?
82.x: Overall BoP positive → adds to reserves; negative → draws them down; the monetary authority is the ultimate financier.

82.s: What is the freedom to convert currency for trade, income and transfers called?
82.x: Current account convertibility – Trade, income and transfers (current international transactions)

82.s: Which type: Investment and financial assets (FDI, portfolio, borrowing) without capital controls?
82.x: Capital account convertibility – Investment and financial assets (FDI, portfolio, borrowing) without capital controls

82.s: On which account is the rupee fully convertible?
82.x: The rupee is fully convertible only on the current account; capital account convertibility is still partial, and the rupee does not convert into gold.

82.s: Which IMF Article makes current account convertibility obligatory?
82.x: IMF Article VIII makes current account convertibility obligatory; India accepted it in August 1994 (operationalised 19 Aug 1994).

82.s: In which year was FERA enacted to prevent outflow of foreign exchange?
82.x: 1973 – FERA (prevent outflow of foreign exchange)

82.s: In which year: Rupee delinked from pound sterling, pegged to a basket of currencies?
82.x: Sep 1975 – Rupee delinked from pound sterling, pegged to a basket of currencies

82.x: July 1991 – Rupee devalued in two steps (1 and 3 July) – about 22% – to meet the BoP crisis

o: A dual exchange rate (40% official, 60% market)
A fixed peg to the dollar

82.s: In which year: Unified, market-determined exchange rate (trade account convertibility)?
82.x: 1 Mar 1993 – Unified, market-determined exchange rate (trade account convertibility)

82.x: Aug 1994 – Full current account convertibility – Article VIII accepted

82.x: 1999 / 1 June 2000 – FEMA enacted / in force, replacing FERA

82.s: Which law's preamble aims "to facilitate external trade and payments"?
82.x: FEMA preamble: "to facilitate external trade and payments" and promote orderly development of the forex market.

82.s: What was the nature of offences under FERA?
82.x: Nature – Criminal – Civil

82.s: What is the nature of offences under FEMA?
82.x: Nature – Criminal – Civil

82.s: What was the approach of FERA towards foreign exchange?
82.x: Approach – Control of outflow – Management and regulation

82.s: What is the approach of FEMA towards foreign exchange?
82.x: Approach – Control of outflow – Management and regulation

82.s: How is the character of FERA described?
82.x: Character – Strict, restrictive – Liberal

82.s: How is the character of FEMA described?
82.x: Character – Strict, restrictive – Liberal

82.s: Who chaired the High Level Committee on Balance of Payments (1991-93)?

82.x: High Level Committee on BoP (1991-93) – C. Rangarajan – Sustainable CAD about 1.6% of GDP; market-determined exchange rate

82.s: Who chaired the Committee on Capital Account Convertibility (1997)?
82.x: Committee on Capital Account Convertibility (1997) – S.S. Tarapore – Roadmap to fuller capital account convertibility; preconditions: fiscal consolidation, inflation, strong banks

82.x: Committee on Fuller CAC (2006) – S.S. Tarapore – Revisited the roadmap

82.s: What did the 2006 Committee on Fuller Capital Account Convertibility do?
82.x: Committee on Fuller CAC (2006) – S.S. Tarapore – Revisited the roadmap

82.s: Which is an expenditure-switching measure to correct a BoP deficit?
82.x: Export incentives, tourist promotion – Foreign loans, IMF assistance, foreign investment (FDI); exchange control

82.s: What does higher government spending on domestic projects do to the current account deficit?
82.x: Steps that worsen the deficit – Levying higher export duties (cuts exports); increasing government spending on domestic projects (raises demand and imports)

82.s: What does encouraging FDI do for a current account deficit?
82.x: Encouraging FDI – *Finances* a deficit rather than correcting it

82.s: Which step helps reduce a current account deficit?
82.x: Reducing CAD – Devaluing the currency and attracting FDI/FII funds help; cutting export subsidies hurts exports

82.s: Which step removes a BoP surplus when demand is elastic?
82.x: Removing a BoP surplus (elastic demand) – Appreciate/revalue the currency; devaluation, import controls or inflation abroad would widen the surplus

82.s: What does a large current-account surplus give a country?
o: Capacity to give aid and loans abroad
82.x: Large current-account surplus – Larger capacity to give aid and loans abroad

82.s: How many times was the rupee devalued in July 1991?
82.x: 1991 – Rupee devalued twice (1 and 3 July 1991) to adjust the BoP deficit

82.s: What kind of steps were the May 2026 appeal to cut gold and fuel imports and the gold duty hike?
82.x: May 2026 – Appeal to cut gold and fuel imports + gold import-duty hike = expenditure-switching steps

82.x: Rekhi Committee (1992) – Indirect taxes

82.x: Rangarajan – BoP

82.s: What did the Goiporia Committee deal with?
82.x: Goiporia – Bank customer service

82.s: What is the main function of the IMF?
o: Helping members solve balance of payments problems
82.x: IMF main function – Help members solve balance of payments problems; loans meet temporary BoP deficits (development projects are the World Bank's work)

82.s: What is the core function of the IMF over members' economic policies?
82.x: Core function – Surveillance

82.x: Role – Lender of last resort when reserves cannot cover a deficit; India drew on the IMF in 1991

82.s: What is a member's reserve (gold) tranche in the IMF?
o: An unconditional drawing right from its quota
A gold deposit with the World Bank
82.x: Reserve (gold) tranche – Member's unconditional drawing right from its quota – a credit system of the IMF

82.s: To whom does the IMF's Rapid Financing Instrument give help for urgent BoP needs?
82.x: Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI) – Rapid help for any member with an urgent BoP need

82.s: For which countries is the IMF's concessional Rapid Credit Facility meant?
82.x: Rapid Credit Facility (RCF) – Concessional, for low-income countries

82.s: What are the IMF's Stand-By Arrangement and Extended Fund Facility?
82.x: Stand-By Arrangement / Extended Fund Facility – Regular lending windows

82.s: Which of these is not an IMF instrument?
82.x: RBI swaps, the SAARC swap framework and Special Rupee Vostro Accounts are outside the IMF's instruments.

82.x: SDR – IMF reserve asset ("paper gold", 1969); exists only as book-keeping entries – neither paper currency nor metal

82.s: What should a country avoid depending on to be immune to a global financial crisis?

82.s: Which of these lowers India's currency-crisis risk?

83.s: What does devaluation do to a country's exports abroad?
83.x: Effect on prices – Devaluation makes exports cheaper abroad (their foreign-currency price falls) and imports dearer at home

83.s: Why does devaluation promote exports?
o: The price of the country's products abroad falls
83.x: Result – It promotes exports – because the price of the country's products in the international market falls

83.s: What type of policy is devaluation?
83.x: Policy type – An expenditure-switching policy (spending switches to home-produced goods)

83.s: Which of these is devaluation not meant to do?
83.x: Purpose – To correct the balance of trade / BoP; it raises the cost of imports and does not curb inflation

83.s: What does devaluation necessarily do?
83.x: What it does necessarily – Only improves export competitiveness – it does not necessarily improve the trade balance or raise the currency's foreign value

83.s: Which of these is a limit of devaluation?
83.x: Limits – Imported inflation (it raises domestic prices), inelastic oil imports, costlier ECB repayment

83.s: When does devaluation work?
o: When domestic prices rise to match
When exports actually become cheaper to importers abroad
83.x: When does it work? – When exports actually become cheaper to importers abroad – export prices fall in proportion to the devaluation and domestic prices do not rise to cancel it

83.s: Why was the rupee devalued in 1991?
83.x: 1991 – The rupee was devalued to make exports cheaper; export growth rose after 1991 and the devaluation is credited for it

83.s: What are import duties, exchange controls and devaluation used to do to a trade imbalance?
83.x: Import duties, exchange controls and devaluation are used to wipe out the trade imbalance and keep the rate stable.

83.s: Which of these is a method of correcting a BoP deficit?
83.x: BoP correction methods: monetary policy, exchange depreciation, devaluation, exchange control, import duties and quotas, export promotion, foreign loans and investment.

83.s: What is the price of one currency in terms of another called?
83.x: Exchange rate – The price / value of one currency in terms of another (₹50 for $1 = ₹50 per dollar)

83.s: Which of these is a participant in the forex market?
83.x: Forex market participants – Commercial banks, brokers, authorised dealers, monetary authorities

83.s: By whom is foreign exchange for imports sanctioned, through authorised dealers under FEMA?
83.x: Forex for imports – Sanctioned by the RBI (through authorised dealers, under FEMA)

83.s: What is a quote giving units of domestic currency per unit of foreign currency (₹95 = $1) called?
83.x: Direct quote – Units of domestic currency per one unit of foreign currency (₹95 = $1)

83.s: What is a quote giving units of foreign currency per unit of domestic currency called?
83.x: Indirect quote – Units of foreign currency per one unit of domestic currency

83.s: How many days does a spot foreign exchange deal take to settle?
83.x: Spot rate – Immediate delivery – settled within two days

83.s: What does an importer's forward contract cover?
83.x: Forward rate – Agreed now for future delivery; an importer's forward contract covers exchange-rate risk

83.s: What is covering exchange risk through forward contracts called?
83.x: Hedging / speculation – Covering exchange risk (forwards) / taking an open position on expected moves

83.s: What is buying a currency where it is cheaper and selling it where it is dearer called?
83.x: Arbitrage – Buying a currency where it is cheaper and simultaneously selling it where it is dearer

83.s: What is foreign money that moves quickly between markets for short-term returns called?
83.x: Hot currency (money) – Foreign currency that migrates quickly between markets for the highest short-term return

83.s: What is the Tobin tax levied on?
83.x: Tobin tax – Tax on foreign exchange transactions (James Tobin)

83.s: What is it called when countries competitively devalue their currencies for export advantage?
83.x: Currency war – Countries competitively devaluing their currencies to gain export advantage

83.s: What is hawala?
o: Illegal transfer of foreign exchange outside banks
83.x: Hawala – Illegal transactions of foreign exchange (informal transfer outside banking channels)

83.s: What does money laundering turn into apparently legal money?
83.x: Money laundering – Turns the proceeds of crime (drugs, smuggling, corruption) into apparently legal money; hawala is a common channel

83.s: About how many months of import cover did India's forex reserves give in January 2026 (Economic Survey 2025-26)?
83.x: Import cover – The number of months of imports that could be paid for by the country's reserves – about 11 months with $701.4 bn (16 Jan 2026, Economic Survey 2025-26)

83.s: What is the international liquidity problem a shortage of?
83.x: International liquidity problem – Shortage of dollars and other hard currencies (internationally accepted reserve assets)

83.s: Which is the most valuable currency in rupee terms?
83.x: Most valuable currency (in ₹): Kuwaiti dinar; of pound, euro and US dollar the costliest is the pound sterling (₹125.18 vs euro ₹109.05, $ ₹93.00 on 17 Apr 2026).

83.s: When did the RBI announce its framework for settling international trade in rupees?

83.s: Where may surplus balances in Special Rupee Vostro Accounts be invested since 2025?

83.s: What is a Vostro account?
o: A foreign bank's account with a domestic bank
83.x: Vostro / Nostro – Foreign bank's account with a domestic bank / ours abroad
